Chapter 10: Sustaining Growth and Embracing the Ongoing Journey
Healing from the legacy of toxic parents isn’t something you just check off a list. It’s not a straight path—there’ll be days when old wounds pop up, or you might second-guess yourself.
The real secret? Learning to see this journey as ongoing. It means offering yourself compassion, and being patient as you move forward, no matter how many twists and turns life throws your way.
So, how do you actually sustain that growth? It’s all about putting your skills and insights into practice, day by day.
Start with regular self-reflection. Ask yourself—how am I really feeling? What do I need right now? Are my boundaries holding up?
And don’t be afraid to ask for support. Whether it’s friends, a therapist, or a support group, reaching out when you hit a rough patch is a sign of strength, not weakness.
Sometimes, as you grow, your boundaries will need a little adjusting. That’s perfectly normal. It’s okay to revisit and even revise your limits as you change. Growth isn’t static—it moves with you.
And please, don’t forget to celebrate your resilience. Think about how much work it takes to break out of old patterns and create something new for yourself. That’s no small thing.
Here’s something to pay attention to—healing doesn’t mean erasing your past or reaching some magical place where everything’s perfect. Instead, it’s about building a life that feels true to you, where you’re no longer held back by old pain.
There’ll still be days when grief, anger, or longing sneak up on you. That’s just being human. It doesn’t mean you’ve failed. Each time you choose self-compassion and make healthier choices, you’re reinforcing new habits and reminding yourself that you’re in control now.
Over time, you’ll notice the pain from the past holds less and less power over you. What takes its place is a hard-won sense of self—capable, worthy, and absolutely deserving of love.
So, as you keep moving forward, remember: this journey is yours. You get to shape it, one step at a time.
